ratings.note: Every tool page on the critical journey; the evidence (375 loan-open) shows the fixed bar covering content, a minor delay; recurs each visit. s=2.
Every add on a phone; the toast is gone by 2.5 s and the basket count is off-screen, so the way on is unclear but recoverable by scrolling up; infrequent members meet it again. s=3.

Every basket visit has the row-reverse session list (and the find page has the reordered search); focus moves against the layout, which invites a wrong pick that the confirm summary can still catch; recurs. s=3.

Every reservation makes the decision twice, with an avoidable error and a card date that can contradict the session (probes 36, 52). s=4, rated 3 because the error is caught and recoverable before commit and the confirm page shows the session; it is not release-blocking.
Only phone users of the date filter; the result changes above the viewport, so they retry or scroll; recurs on each change. s=2.
The screenshot shows the sessions latest-first on every basket visit; scanning for the wanted Saturday is slowed and the wrong week is possible, but it shows again on confirm; recurs. s=3.
Desktop basket only; the screenshot shows one wide card over five tiles, which is uneven but every label is readable; the ordering harm is rated in the reversed-order findings. s=1.
Every page carries the generic masthead; no task effect is shown; it is a brand-fit matter only. s=1.
The grid has no month caption; confusion is likely only near a month boundary, and the status line names the month after a choice; minor doubt that recurs. s=2.
Hits members on the change-session journey who typed details first (probes 18, 36, 51); three fields are wiped, which may surface only as errors at Confirm; happens on every round trip. s=3.
Keyboard-only members on every tool page; up to 21 Tab stops and arrows do nothing, which is tedious but passable; not overcome by learning. s=2.
Only members who open filters see the native yyyy/mm/dd field and the default select; a brief format mismatch that a date picker resolves; mostly visual. s=1.
Every add at desktop width; the toast covers the 'We' header for about a second; no task effect. s=1.
Every basket visit shows the sessions latest-first, against calendar order; scanning is slower and the wrong week is possible but visible on confirm; recurs. s=3.

Every completed reservation leaves 'Basket (1)' next to 'Reservation confirmed', and the basket still offers the drill (probe 21). The explicit confirmation limits the confusion, but a duplicate is possible; it persists until removed by hand. s=3.
The 375 screenshot shows search and filters after all ten cards on every phone visit; members with a tool in mind must scroll the list, a delay not a block; not learned by infrequent members. s=3.
Keyboard and magnifier users above 480 px; focus reaches the results before the search shown above them; disorienting each visit. s=2.

Both drill cards read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...' on phones (screenshot), on the primary example task; it means extra navigation or the wrong drill, recoverable from the tool heading and the basket card; every visit. s=3.
Members who pause mid-reservation (common per context) are not told the hold is limited; they may lose a one-of-a-kind tool believing it is held; recurs. s=3.
In dark mode the green badges lose their pill shape (screenshot); the text still reads; a coherence problem only (contrast is rated in B-018). s=1.
Every done page shows FT-4471 beside membership format FT-01234; only some members will quote the wrong one, costing the desk a little time; recurs. s=2.
Every reservation; the first Saturday read is the 24th; a wrong-week pick is possible but is restated on confirm; recurs. s=3.
The same latest-first session list on every basket visit (screenshot); slows finding the nearest session and invites a wrong pick; recurs. s=3.
On the tool details, two value-column offsets are visible; every value is still readable; cosmetic. s=1.

15 of 21 days are non-session days and look selectable; first-time members do not know the session days; Monday 12 is accepted silently and carried to the basket (probes 2, 5, 16), leading to a later failure; recurs. s=3.
Desktop and tablet basket; the grid is ragged and wraps to three lines, but every option stays readable and selectable. s=1.
Every desktop done page shows 'Basket (1)' after confirmation; mixed status with some duplicate risk; persists until removed. s=3.
Every phone page; nav labels wrap and the masthead is tall; still usable. s=1.

Any unmatched query, including members' own words such as 'drill with two batteries' (probe 56), shows all ten tools with an empty status; this misleads sighted and screen-reader users alike; recurs on each such search. s=3.
Only screen-reader users of the date filter; the 'Available from' label conveys most of the meaning, so the missing hint is minor; every visit. s=1.
Every phone visit; both drills are truncated to the same text (screenshot); risk of opening the wrong one, recoverable on the tool page; recurs. s=3.
Every page has a generic identity; no task effect is evidenced; appeal and brand only. s=1.
Members wanting the date filter (core task 3) meet an unlabelled icon button; the filter may go unused, but cards show dates; learnable. s=2.
Members at 320 px or high zoom (older members, larger text common) get a 330 px minimum column that overflows by about 42 px on the main list, a reflow failure; not overcome. s=3.
Screen-reader users who press Reserve before choosing a day hear only a date name; the error is neither live nor described (probe 60), a silent failure on the critical step; recurs. s=3.
Only members reserving four or more tools; a fourth is accepted with a GBP 95 deposit (probes 50, 52) and the member learns at the desk that it will not be lent; once per reservation. s=2.
Short desktop pages show a grey band below the footer; purely visual. s=1.

Members who plan while doing something else (the declared scene) easily pass 10 minutes; the hold silently lapses and the flow fails at Continue, a WCAG 2.2.1 failure that blocks the critical task; not signalled on later visits either. s=4.
Date-filter users; the hint promises 'on or after' but later-available tools are hidden (probe 11), so members may misjudge what is lendable; recurs. s=2.
Only after a failed Continue followed by removing every tool; a stale error that cannot be acted on, with 'Find a tool' present; it ends on leaving the page. s=1.
The grey band under the footer on short desktop pages is visual only. s=1.
Screen-reader members navigating by heading get twelve flat level-2 headings on find and basket; the grouping is lost, which is a minor slowdown; every visit. s=2.

Only when a held tool's availability is later than the chosen session (3 of 10 tools); the basket proceeds to confirm with Saturday 10 (probe 52), risking a wasted trip; carried into the reservation. s=3.

Tools available later than the first days (about 4 of 10); 10 October is accepted for a 17 October tool (probe 34), so the member may arrive for a tool that is still out; recurs per such reservation. s=3.
Every basket offers sessions before the chosen day without comment; a mild contradiction that a careful reader sees on the card. s=2.
Every Reserve; the toast hides after about 1.3 s regardless of hover (verifier frames), so members glancing away miss the only nearby feedback; recurs. s=3.
Every phone visit to find; search is below the ten cards, so finding a known tool is slowed, not blocked; not learned by infrequent members. s=3.
At desktop width the session cards break into one wide and five cramped; still readable and selectable; the ordering is rated separately. s=1.
Only on accidental removal; it empties the basket with no undo (probes 37, 55, 59), and recovering takes several steps while the one-of-a-kind stock is at risk; once per mistake. s=2.
Some first-time members will take 'Reserve this tool' plus 'Added to your basket' as done; then nothing is set aside, so the task fails; usually learned after one miss. s=3.
Phone users who open the loan list see only 'One week' and the focused option hidden under the bar (probe 107 down.png); a minor obstacle; recurs. s=2.
Any no-match search shows the full list with no empty-state message (screenshot), so members may think the tool is stocked or search failed; recurs. s=3.
Few members use forced colours at narrow widths, but for them the 320 forced-colours capture shows no session markers, so they may pick a closed day; not overcome. s=3.
Every desktop add shows the toast briefly over the 'We' header; cosmetic. s=1.
Members who type only the card digits get a generic 'Enter your membership number' error (probes 10, 38); the example shows the fix; once learned it is gone. s=2.
Every reservation passes the reversed session group; focus moves up-left against the visual order (probes 26, 66), inviting a wrong-week pick that confirm restates; recurs. s=3.
The jagged value column on the tool details is still readable; cosmetic. s=1.
Every reservation has two 1.2-1.5 s waits with no visible change (probe 13), which invites repeat taps (see the duplicate-booking finding); recurs. s=3.

A single column of about 610 px on short read/confirm pages is a sound line length for these users; the empty right side does not hinder any task or comprehension, so I do not see a usability problem.
Screen-reader members navigating by landmark may miss Reserve, which sits outside main; it is still reached in reading order, so this is a minor delay; every visit. s=2.
At desktop width the Reserve button is about 80 px off the content column; an alignment issue with no task effect. s=1.
The calendar has no month or year label; doubt arises mainly near month ends, and chosen dates are later spelled out; recurs. s=2.

Dark mode is common and most cards carry the green badge at about 3.1:1 (screenshot shows dim green), below 4.5:1 for the availability date that drives the choice; older members cannot overcome low contrast. s=3.
Members whose phones autofill +44 get a contradictory error (probe 53) and must reformat; one retry each time. s=2.
Keyboard and switch users who open the loan list cannot Tab or Escape out until they choose (verifier probe), a WCAG 2.1.2 trap on the critical step; escape by selection can be learned. s=3.
Screen-reader users on every tool page hear 'One week, button' with no label; the region name gives some context, so the choice is unclear but workable; not overcome. s=2.
Closed days (15 of 21) are accepted until Confirm, after the 1.5 s wait, with an unlinked error (vp1-03), so the member must go back three steps; recurs for members unaware of the session days. s=3.
Every phone visit; search sits about 2000 px down and the first viewport gives no hint (s01-home), which slows a member looking for one tool; infrequent use means it is not learned. s=3.

Whenever the hold has expired, Continue always fails with 'Something went wrong. Try again.', including after reload (vp1-10), a dead end on the critical journey; it persists until storage is cleared. s=4.
Every phone visit shows both drills with identical truncated titles; risk of the wrong drill, recoverable on the tool page; recurs. s=3.
Every card has an identical wrench tile; it adds no information but the names and categories still distinguish tools; appeal only. s=1.
Every add; after the toast the page is unchanged and there is no onward link (probe 39), so first-time members may press again or leave; recoverable via the header; recurs. s=3.
Nav labels wrap on every phone page (probe 107 shows it); usable; cosmetic. s=1.
The placeholder wrench appears on all cards; no information loss beyond visual recognition aid; appeal and trust only. s=1.

Double taps are common on touch, and the 1.5 s with no visible busy state invites them; each one allocates a second reservation (FT-4471 and FT-4472 on done, probe 88), tying up one-of-a-kind stock and needing the desk to sort it out. s=4.
